# Remount

> Remount is a runtime for AI agents that need a real computer rather than a function call.

Remount is an open protocol and a single static Go binary that gives an AI
agent a workspace it can run on from anywhere: snapshotted, moved between
machines, put to sleep, and reattached within session retention limits.
Broker-managed provider keys stay outside it; explicit workspace login is
a separate trust choice. `remount run RECIPE -- TASK` launches a coding harness in one
command. The normative wire protocol is [spec/PROTOCOL.md](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/spec/PROTOCOL.md).

## README

- [What you can do with it](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#what-you-can-do-with-it): again, `attach`, and read the output you missed.
- [How it differs from a sandbox API](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#how-it-differs-from-a-sandbox-api): Most sandbox products give you a container behind an HTTP API in someone else's cloud.
- [How it fits together](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#how-it-fits-together): Every machine that runs workspaces is a node.
- [Quick start](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#quick-start): You need the Go version in `go.mod` (1.27.1 at the time of writing).
- [Move a workspace](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#move-a-workspace): The filesystem is snapshotted, the workspace is re-queued, a node in that zone picks it up, and your files are there.
- [Sleep and wake](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#sleep-and-wake): A sleeping workspace has no node.
- [Keep a workspace awake for background work](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#keep-a-workspace-awake-for-background-work): `ws sleep` means sleep now.
- [Credentials](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#credentials): Define a binding once, on the server:
- [Isolation](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#isolation): A runtime profile is a promise a node makes at startup, and the node refuses to start if it cannot keep it.
- [Browser](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#browser): A computer is a browser the node drives inside a workspace.
- [Events](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#events): Every state change writes an event in the same transaction as the state.
- [Commands](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#commands): Ctrl-C in `exec`, `sh` or `attach` detaches and prints the `attach` command that picks the process back up.
- [Go SDK](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#go-sdk): Import the public packages, not `internal/`:
- [Observability](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#observability): All three take `--json`.
- [Repository layout](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#repository-layout): `internal/` is not a supported import path.
- [Documentation](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#documentation)
- [Status and limits](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#status-and-limits): Everything above is implemented and tested, including under the race detector and in the one-process simulator with fault injection.
- [License](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/README.md#license): Apache-2.0.

## Using Remount

- [Choose the workflow](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#choose-the-workflow)
- [Build and select a server](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#build-and-select-a-server): From an accessible repository checkout, with the Go version required by `go.mod` (currently 1.27.1):
- [Run a coding agent on a checkout](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#run-a-coding-agent-on-a-checkout): The shortest local path is:
- [Operate a durable Agent](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#operate-a-durable-agent): An Agent owns a workspace and a durable transcript.
- [Retrieve modified files](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#retrieve-modified-files): Agent changes live in the workspace, not automatically in the original host checkout.
- [Use workspace primitives directly](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#use-workspace-primitives-directly): Start a manual local deployment:
- [Run browser and virtual desktop workloads](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#run-browser-and-virtual-desktop-workloads): A browser is a protocol resource — a computer session, driven by the node.
- [Broker provider credentials](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#broker-provider-credentials): Provider keys belong in the control plane, never in a workspace.
- [Deploy the Modal reference](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#deploy-the-modal-reference): `deploy/modal_app.py` is a reference deployment of one control plane and one process-backend node in one Modal container.
- [Choose a runtime profile](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#choose-a-runtime-profile): A runtime profile is a machine's isolation claim, enforced as a fail-closed startup gate on the node and as a scheduling constraint on the workspace, and answered three-valued by `doctor --profile` and `conformance --profile`.
- [Provider-backed nodes are not credential checks](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#provider-backed-nodes-are-not-credential-checks): Fly, E2B, Modal, ix.dev, and SSH pool drivers create whole Remount nodes.
- [Verify outcomes and clean up](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#verify-outcomes-and-clean-up): Use the resource state and durable evidence, not a successful client call alone:
- [Public API, errors and tracing](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#public-api-errors-and-tracing): Remount's public surface is the Go `api` and `client` packages, the `remount` Python package, the `@remount/sdk` npm package, the wire protocol, and the documented CLI flags and `--json` shapes.
- [Documentation map and maintenance](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/using-remount.md#documentation-map-and-maintenance): This guide owns the supported **user journeys**.

## Tutorial

- [1. Build](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#1-build): The core is one Go binary; selected backends and harness recipes have additional runtime prerequisites.
- [2. One command](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#2-one-command): If you have a provider key in your environment, the whole thing is one command.
- [3. Start standalone by hand and run a command](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#3-start-standalone-by-hand-and-run-a-command): `remount standalone` runs the control plane, the relay and one node in a single process.
- [4. An interactive shell](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#4-an-interactive-shell): `remount sh` opens a session of kind `pty`.
- [5. The filesystem](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#5-the-filesystem): Every filesystem operation is served by the node and jailed to the workspace root.
- [6. Reconnect without losing output](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#6-reconnect-without-losing-output): Start a command that runs for a while, then kill the client half way through.
- [7. A second machine, and a move](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#7-a-second-machine-and-a-move): On another computer, enroll it as a node.
- [8. Sleep and wake](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#8-sleep-and-wake): A sleeping workspace has no node.
- [9. Secrets the workspace never holds](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#9-secrets-the-workspace-never-holds): Stop the standalone process and write a bindings file.
- [10. Watch everything](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#10-watch-everything): Transactional resource rows are the source of lifecycle/recovery truth.
- [Where to go next](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/tutorial.md#where-to-go-next)

## Harness integration

- [`remount run`: one command from a checkout to a working agent](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#remount-run-one-command-from-a-checkout-to-a-working-agent): `run` creates a workspace from `--dir` (or `--base NAME`, or reuses `--ws WS`), installs the harness if the image lacks it, writes a launcher under `.remount/launch/`, and opens a session that runs it.
- [Browser and virtual desktop workloads](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#browser-and-virtual-desktop-workloads): For a browser, reach for the built-in computer session first: `remount computer` and the SDK `Computer` handles drive screenshots, input, navigation and downloads as protocol operations, against the reference image in [`images/browser`](../images/browser/Dockerfile).
- [Verified: OpenAI Codex CLI](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#verified-openai-codex-cli): We ran Codex CLI 0.152.1 inside a Remount workspace on macOS with the `process` backend.
- [The general pattern for any harness](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#the-general-pattern-for-any-harness): Every harness has a variable for where the model lives and a variable for the key.
- [HTTP_PROXY mode](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#http_proxy-mode): The broker is also an ordinary HTTP forward proxy.
- [Repositories: the git connector and the `/d/` stopgap](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#repositories-the-git-connector-and-the-d-stopgap): Two ways exist to reach a repository from a workspace.
- [Writing your own loop](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#writing-your-own-loop): The supported Go SDK is `remount.dev/remount/client`; its stable resource model and error codes are in `remount.dev/remount/api`.
- [What a harness gets for free](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/harness-integration.md#what-a-harness-gets-for-free): Truthful bounded replay.

## Agent HTTP API

- [Base URL, authentication, errors](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#base-url-authentication-errors): Every route is under the server's base URL (`--public-url` when set).
- [Usage](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#usage): `GET /v1/usage?tenant=&ws=&principal=&binding=&window=` translates to `usage.get` and returns `UsageRes{usage}`.
- [Agents](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#agents): `Agent`, `AgentCreateReq`, `AgentSpec` and `AgentPolicy` are the protocol types serialized as JSON with their `json` tags; the request to create an agent from a recipe is:
- [Transcript](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#transcript): `GET /v1/agents/{id}/transcript?from=N&limit=M` reads the durable mirror (§6.2) as a page:
- [Approvals](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#approvals): Decision validation is per kind (§6.1): a `tool_call` takes one of the offered `options`, an `elicitation` takes `content` (a JSON object) or `denied`, an `egress` takes `allow`/`deny`.
- [Diff](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#diff): `GET /v1/agents/{id}/diff[?wake=true]` returns
- [Terminal](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#terminal): `GET /v1/agents/{id}/terminal` upgrades to a WebSocket that is the xterm.js endpoint.
- [Files](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#files): `/v1/agents/{id}/fs/{path}` is the workspace filesystem, jailed by the node (§7).
- [Preview proxy](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#preview-proxy): `/v1/agents/{id}/ports/{port}/{rest}` is an authenticated reverse proxy to TCP `{port}` inside the workspace, the same forward `remount port` uses, for HTTP and WebSocket traffic.
- [Webhooks](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#webhooks): `POST /v1/events` takes `{type, stream?, payload?, agent?}` and appends the event.
- [Scheduling and children](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#scheduling-and-children): `policy.start_at` (Unix milliseconds) holds the first run until that time: the agent is `scheduled`, its workspace is ready, and messages queue.
- [Bounds](https://github.com/andrewgcodes/remount/blob/main/docs/api.md#bounds): Every bound is a `4xx`/`5xx` with a stable code, never a truncated success.
